title: Discount vacation package
pretext: a seven-night resort vacation you've been selected for
story: The caller says the resident was selected for a seven-night resort package worth $4,000 for only $199 in port taxes and fees. The offer must be booked today, and later the caller adds more fees.
ask: Pay $199 in taxes and fees today by reading your card number, then give your passport details to reserve the trip.

red_flags.cue: A travel company calls about a trip the resident never asked about.
Taxes and fees must be paid before any details are provided in writing.
The offer is only good if booked on this call.
The caller asks for a card number and passport details.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}}, say you're with Sunmere Vacation Club, and that they've been selected for a seven-night resort stay.
stages.build_trust: Sound excited. Describe the beach, the included meals, and the flexible dates.
stages.ask: Explain that only $199 in taxes and fees is due today and ask for their card number and passport details to reserve.
stages.pressure: Say the offer ends when the call ends and several other callers are waiting for the last spots.
stages.close: Take the payment, then mention a 'resort fee' that also has to be paid now.

disclosure_triggers: starts reading a card number, expiration date, or security code
gives their Social Security number or date of birth
pass_signals: asks for the offer in writing before paying anything
says they'll look up the company and its reviews first
refuses to pay on an unexpected call

difficulty.easy: Asks for the card number almost immediately and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Describes the trip for a few turns before the ask. Answers one objection with the employee ID and booking code before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Enthusiastic and flexible. Promises a written confirmation by email after payment, offers the callback number, and lowers the fee when challenged. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
